title_en: Yang Yimin v. Chengdu Municipal Government — other administrative dispute
ruling_gist_en: A reply to a petition made by an administrative organ in response to a party's appeal, which rejects the party's petition, constitutes a repetitive handling act by the administrative organ regarding the party's challenge to an administrative act. It does not produce any new legal effect on the party's rights and obligations and is not an administrative act subject to application for administrative reconsideration as stipulated in the Administrative Reconsideration Law. Where a party, dissatisfied with the aforesaid reply to a petition, applies for administrative reconsideration, and the administrative reconsideration organ that accepts the application renders a decision not to accept the case, and the party, dissatisfied with that decision, files a lawsuit with the people's court requesting the court to annul the decision not to accept the case, the people's court will not support such a claim.
keywords_en: Administration; Rejection of Administrative Reconsideration Application; First Instance; Intermediate People's Court; Sichuan Province; Natural Person; State Organ; Administrative Reconsideration Law; Regulations on Letters and Visits; Whether a Reply to a Petition Falls Within the Scope of Administrative Reconsideration; Reviewability of Repetitive Handling Acts; Dismissal of Claims; Petition Appeal; Removal from Roster; Rejection of Administrative Reconsideration Application; Administrative Litigation; Other Administrative Disputes v. Chengdu Municipal Government
full_text_en:
Yang Yimin v. Chengdu Municipal People's Government — Other Administrative Dispute

Ruling Summary

A reply to a petition from an administrative organ which dismisses a party's appeal against an administrative act is a repetitive act by the administrative organ in response to the party's complaint regarding the administrative act, and does not create any new legal effect on the party's rights and obligations. It is not an administrative act for which an application for administrative reconsideration may be filed under the Administrative Reconsideration Law. Where a party, dissatisfied with the aforesaid petition reply from the administrative organ, applies for administrative reconsideration, and the administrative reconsideration organ receiving the application makes a decision of non-acceptance, and the party, dissatisfied with that decision, files a lawsuit requesting the people's court to annul the decision of non-acceptance, the people's court shall not support the claim.

Plaintiff: Yang Yimin, male, 52 years old, residing at Luojiayan Street, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province.

Defendant: Chengdu Municipal People's Government, Sichuan Province, domiciled at: Renmin West Road, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Ge Honglin, Mayor of the City.

Plaintiff Yang Yimin filed an administrative lawsuit with the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court, Sichuan Province, against the defendant, the Chengdu Municipal People's Government (hereinafter referred to as the Chengdu Municipal Government), arising from another administrative dispute.

Plaintiff Yang Yimin alleged: The plaintiff was an employee of the former Chengdu No. 5 Middle School (now Chengdu Liewu Middle School). The school refused to assign work to the plaintiff or pay his salary on the grounds that he had already been "expelled" in 1992, and also forcibly confiscated the plaintiff's housing, but failed to deliver the relevant processing documents to the plaintiff for a long time. These acts seriously infringed upon the plaintiff's personal and property rights. For this reason, the plaintiff filed a complaint with the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau in 2005. The Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau, in the name of its office, made a petition reply to the plaintiff on May 20, 2005, stating that the former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission (the predecessor of the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau) had already issued the "Reply to the 'Report on the Expulsion of Our Employee Yang Yimin' from Chengdu No. 5 Middle School" in 1992, and considered that this reply complied with legal provisions. The plaintiff, dissatisfied, appealed to the Sichuan Provincial Education Department, which ordered the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau to review the matter. The Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau again gave the plaintiff a petition reply on August 18, 2005, with the same content as the previous reply. The plaintiff, still dissatisfied with this petition reply, filed an application for administrative reconsideration with the defendant, the Chengdu Municipal Government, on September 9, 2005, requesting the Chengdu Municipal Government to conduct administrative reconsideration regarding the matters involved in that petition reply. After receiving the reconsideration application, the Chengdu Municipal Government considered that the plaintiff's application did not meet the acceptance conditions for administrative reconsideration and, on September 13, 2005, issued the Decision of Non-Acceptance No. 6 [2005] of the Chengdu Municipal Government (Chengfu Fu Bu Zi (2005) No. 6). The plaintiff believes that the petition reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau to the plaintiff was a decision on his complaint with the nature of administrative confirmation and administrative disposition, which had a serious impact on the plaintiff's personal and property rights, and was not merely a "clarification or explanation." Therefore, the plaintiff's application for administrative reconsideration filed with the Chengdu Municipal Government in accordance with the law fully falls within the scope of cases acceptable for administrative reconsideration as stipulated in Article 6, items (9) and (11) of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Administrative Reconsideration Law). The Chengdu Municipal Government, without correctly explaining the reasons and legal basis to the plaintiff, made a decision of non-acceptance for a case that obviously could be subject to administrative reconsideration under the law, thereby neglecting the right of remedy granted to citizens by the Constitution and depriving the plaintiff of the statutory remedy opportunities available to him. This decision of non-acceptance clearly does not conform to the relevant provisions of laws and regulations and contains an obvious error in the application of laws and regulations. Therefore, the plaintiff requests the court to annul the Decision of Non-Acceptance No. 6 [2005] (Chengfu Fu Bu Zi (2005) No. 6) made by the Chengdu Municipal Government.

Defendant, the Chengdu Municipal Government, argued: According to the relevant provisions of the Administrative Reconsideration Law, administrative reconsideration is a system designed to supervise specific administrative acts. Since the matter for which the plaintiff, Yang Yimin, applied for administrative reconsideration was the petition reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau, which is not a specific administrative act of the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau, Yang Yimin's application does not fall within the scope of acceptance for administrative reconsideration under the law. The defendant requests the court to dismiss Yang Yimin's claims in accordance with the law and to uphold the decision of non-acceptance made by the Chengdu Municipal Government regarding Yang Yimin's application for administrative reconsideration.

Within the statutory period for presenting evidence, the defendant, the Chengdu Municipal Government, submitted to the court the relevant evidentiary materials and legal bases for the contested decision of non-acceptance:

1.  The application for administrative reconsideration submitted by the plaintiff, Yang Yimin, to prove that the matter for which Yang Yimin applied for administrative reconsideration with the Chengdu Municipal Government on September 9, 2005, was the petition reply made by the office of the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau on August 18, 2005, in response to Yang Yimin's complaint;
2.  The petition reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau to Yang Yimin on May 20, 2005; the reply letter from the Sichuan Provincial Education Department to Yang Yimin on June 28, 2005; the "Opinions Requesting the Municipal Education Bureau to Re-correctly Handle My Complaint" submitted by Yang Yimin to the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau on June 30, 2005; and the petition reply made by the office of the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau to Yang Yimin on August 18, 2005; to prove that Yang Yimin's reconsideration application did not meet the conditions for accepting administrative reconsideration as prescribed by the Administrative Reconsideration Law;
3.  The Decision of Non-Acceptance No. 6 [2005] (Chengfu Fu Bu Zi (2005) No. 6) made by the Chengdu Municipal Government on September 9, 2005, and the service receipt, to prove that the procedure for making the decision of non-acceptance by the Chengdu Municipal Government was lawful and that the decision was served on Yang Yimin on September 13, 2005;
4.  The provisions of Articles 34 and 35 of the State Council's "Regulations on Letters and Visits" (Xinfang Tiaoli), to prove that Yang Yimin could not apply for administrative reconsideration regarding the petition reply, and his application for administrative reconsideration does not fall within the scope of administrative reconsideration under the law;
5.  The provisions of Articles 1, 6, 11, and 17 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law, to prove that the petition reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau in response to Yang Yimin's complaint was not a specific administrative act for which an application for administrative reconsideration may be filed under the Administrative Reconsideration Law, and that the Decision of Non-Acceptance made by the Chengdu Municipal Government had clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law.

The Chengdu Intermediate People's Court, ex officio, obtained the following evidence:

1.  The "Report on the Expulsion of Our Employee Yang Yimin" submitted to the former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission on October 3, 1992, the contents of which were: the former Chengdu No. 5 Middle School decided to expel the plaintiff, Yang Yimin, pursuant to the provisions of Document Sichuan People's Issue (1984) No. 4 (Chuan Ren Fa (1984) No. 4);
2.  The "Reply to the 'Report on the Expulsion of Our Employee Yang Yimin' from Chengdu No. 5 Middle School" made by the former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission on December 23, 1992, under Document Chengdu Education Personnel (1992) No. 78 (Cheng Jiao Fa Ren (1992) No. 78), which agreed to the expulsion of Yang Yimin.

The Chengdu Intermediate People's Court found in its trial of first instance:

In 1992, the former Chengdu No. 5 Middle School (now Chengdu Liewu Middle School) submitted the "Report on the Expulsion of Our Employee Yang Yimin" to the former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission (now the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau). The former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission issued the Reply (Cheng Jiao Fa Ren (1992) No. 78) on December 23, 1992, agreeing to the expulsion of the plaintiff, Yang Yimin. In 2005, Yang Yimin, due to the above dispute, filed a petition complaint with the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau. The Bureau, in the name of its office, made a petition reply to Yang Yimin on May 20, 2005, stating that the "Reply to the 'Report on the Expulsion of Our Employee Yang Yimin' from Chengdu No. 5 Middle School" made by the former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission in 1992 complied with legal provisions. After receiving this petition reply, Yang Yimin appealed to the Sichuan Provincial Education Department, which instructed the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau to respond to Yang Yimin again. On August 18, 2005, the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau again gave Yang Yimin a petition reply, the content of which was consistent with the previous reply. On September 9, 2005, Yang Yimin applied for administrative reconsideration with the defendant, the Chengdu Municipal Government, regarding the petition reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau on August 18, 2005. The Chengdu Municipal Government made the Decision of Non-Acceptance No. 6 [2005] (Chengfu Fu Bu Zi (2005) No. 6) on September 9, 2005, and served it on Yang Yimin.

The focus of the dispute in this case is: Whether the application for administrative reconsideration filed by the plaintiff, Yang Yimin, with the defendant, the Chengdu Municipal Government, due to his dissatisfaction with the petition reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau, falls within the scope of acceptance for administrative reconsideration.

The Chengdu Intermediate People's Court held in its judgment of first instance:

The former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission (now the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau), in 1992, issued a reply agreeing to the expulsion of the plaintiff, Yang Yimin, by the former Chengdu No. 5 Middle School. Thirteen years later, the plaintiff, Yang Yimin, filed petition complaints about his expulsion successively with the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau and the Sichuan Provincial Education Department. The Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau ultimately made a petition reply in response to Yang Yimin's complaint, stating that the reply made by the former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission had complied with the relevant regulations. Yang Yimin's application for administrative reconsideration filed with the defendant, the Chengdu Municipal Government, due to his dissatisfaction with this petition reply, does not fall within the scope of acceptance for administrative reconsideration.

First, Article 6 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law stipulates: "Citizens, legal persons, or other organizations may apply for administrative reconsideration in accordance with this Law under any of the following circumstances: (1) if they are dissatisfied with a decision on administrative penalties such as a warning, fine, confiscation of illegal gains, confiscation of illegal property, order for suspension of production or business, temporary suspension or revocation of a permit or license, temporary suspension or revocation of a business license, or administrative detention made by an administrative organ; (2) if they are dissatisfied with a decision on administrative compulsory measures such as restriction of personal freedom, or sealing up, distraining, or freezing of property made by an administrative organ; (3) if they are dissatisfied with a decision made by an administrative organ on the alteration, suspension, or revocation of certificates such as permits, licenses, qualification certificates, or competency certificates; (4) if they are dissatisfied with a decision made by an administrative organ on the confirmation of ownership or right to use natural resources such as land, mineral deposits, water flows, forests, mountains, grasslands, wastelands, tidal flats, or sea areas; (5) if they consider that an administrative organ has infringed upon their lawful right to autonomous management; (6) if they consider that an administrative organ has altered or abolished an agricultural contract, thereby infringing upon their lawful rights and interests; (7) if they consider that an administrative organ has illegally raised funds, collected property, imposed fees, or illegally demanded the performance of other obligations; (8) if they consider that they meet the statutory conditions, and have applied to an administrative organ for the issuance of a permit, license, qualification certificate, competency certificate, or other certificate, or have applied to an administrative organ for approval, registration, or other related matters, but the administrative organ has failed to handle it according to law; (9) if they have applied to an administrative organ for the performance of its statutory duty to protect personal rights, property rights, or the right to education, but the administrative organ has failed to perform it according to law; (10) if they have applied to an administrative organ for the payment of pensions, social insurance funds, or minimum subsistence allowances according to law, but the administrative organ has failed to make the payment according to law; (11) if they consider that other specific administrative acts of an administrative organ have infringed upon their lawful rights and interests." The above provisions do not explicitly include within the scope of acceptance for administrative reconsideration the repetitive act of an administrative organ dismissing a party's appeal against an administrative act.

Second, the scope of acceptance for administrative reconsideration should be specific administrative acts made by administrative organs that affect the rights and obligations of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations. In this case, the petition reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau had no new impact on the current status of the plaintiff, Yang Yimin's, rights and obligations, nor did it change the original administrative legal relationship. It constitutes a repetitive act by an administrative organ dismissing a party's appeal against a specific administrative act. When an administrative organ dismisses a party's request for an appeal against a specific administrative act, it is in fact merely informing the party that the specific administrative act is correct and explaining that the party's request for an appeal concerning that specific administrative act should not be supported according to law. A petition reply that dismisses a party's appeal neither changes the original administrative legal relationship nor forms a new administrative legal relationship, and has no new impact on the party's rights and obligations. Therefore, it does not fall within the scope of acceptance for administrative reconsideration.

In conclusion, the Decision of Non-Acceptance for Administrative Reconsideration No. 6 [2005] (Chengfu Fu Bu Zi (2005) No. 6) made by the defendant, the Chengdu Municipal Government, had clear findings of fact, sufficient evidence, correct application of the law, and lawful procedure, and should be upheld.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 54, paragraph (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court rendered judgment on July 21, 2006:

Uphold the Decision of Non-Acceptance for Administrative Reconsideration No. 6 [2005] (Chengfu Fu Bu Zi (2005) No. 6) made by the defendant, the Chengdu Municipal Government.

Court costs of RMB 100 for the first-instance case acceptance fee and other litigation costs of RMB 30, totaling RMB 130, shall be borne by the plaintiff, Yang Yimin.

Yang Yimin, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Sichuan High People's Court. The main grounds for appeal were: 1. The "Report on the Expulsion of Our Employee Yang Yimin" from the former Chengdu No. 5 Middle School and the "Reply to the 'Report on the Expulsion of Our Employee Yang Yimin' from Chengdu No. 5 Middle School" from the former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission, which were referenced in the petition reply made by the office of the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau, were merely internal documents unilaterally prepared and had never been served on the appellant. Therefore, the petition reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau, confirming that the aforementioned internal documents complied with the relevant regulations, did not constitute a repetitive act of an administrative organ dismissing a party's appeal against an administrative act. Furthermore, the subject making the petition reply, the office of the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau, was not the proper entity, constituting an ultra vires act. The first-instance court's finding that the petition reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau constituted a repetitive act of an administrative organ dismissing a party's appeal against an administrative act, having no new impact on the appellant's current status of rights and obligations and not changing the original administrative legal relationship, was a misunderstanding of the concept of a repetitive administrative act. The appellant's application for administrative reconsideration fell within the scope of acceptance for administrative reconsideration under the law, and the appellant's claims should be supported according to law. 2. The evidence obtained ex officio by the first-instance court was not subject to courtroom cross-examination during the trial. The first-instance judgment's reliance on this evidence to establish the facts of the case violated the rules of evidence and trial principles. In summary, the appellant requested the court of second instance to amend the judgment according to law, and to order the appellee, the Chengdu Municipal Government, to accept the appellant's application for administrative reconsideration according to law.

The appellant, Yang Yimin, did not submit new evidence.

The appellee, the Chengdu Municipal Government, argued in its defense: The appellant, Yang Yimin, dissatisfied with the expulsion decision made by the former Chengdu No. 5 Middle School, filed petition complaints with the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau and the Sichuan Provincial Education Department. The office of the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau ultimately made a petition reply to the appellant on August 18, 2005, dismissing his appeal. This act constituted a repetitive act by an administrative organ on the same matter, and was not a specific administrative act for which an application for administrative reconsideration could be filed. The party concerned should seek remedies in accordance with the explicit provisions of the State Council's "Regulations on Letters and Visits." The first-instance judgment upholding the appellee's decision of non-acceptance was correct. The appellee requested the court of second instance to uphold the judgment according to law and to order the appellant to bear the litigation costs.

The appellee, the Chengdu Municipal Government, did not submit new evidence.

The Sichuan High People's Court, after cross-examination in the second instance, held: Article 22 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning Evidence in Administrative Litigation" stipulates: "Under any of the following circumstances, the people's court has the authority to obtain evidence from relevant administrative organs, other organizations, or citizens, pursuant to Article 34, paragraph 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law: (1) where the determination of facts involves national interests, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others; (2) where procedural matters such as the ex officio addition of parties, suspension of proceedings, termination of proceedings, or withdrawal are involved." Evidence 1 and evidence 2 obtained ex officio by the first-instance court did not meet the requirements of the above provisions. Moreover, these pieces of evidence were not collected or used by the appellee, the Chengdu Municipal Government, in the administrative procedure, and were not used by it as the factual basis for making the decision of non-acceptance. The above evidence was also not presented or cross-examined during the first-instance trial. Therefore, the appellant, Yang Yimin's, ground for appeal in this regard was valid, and the above evidence cannot serve as the basis for establishing facts in this case.

The Sichuan High People's Court found in its trial of second instance:

In 2005, the appellant, Yang Yimin, filed a complaint with the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau, alleging that Chengdu Liewu Middle School, under the pretext of having already "expelled" him, failed to assign him work or pay his salary, and also forcibly confiscated his housing, but failed to deliver the relevant processing documents for a long time, thereby infringing upon his personal and property rights. On May 20, 2005, the office of the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau made a petition reply to Yang Yimin. The reply stated that the "Reply to the 'Report on the Expulsion of Our Employee Yang Yimin' from Chengdu No. 5 Middle School" made by the former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission in 1992 complied with legal provisions. Yang Yimin, dissatisfied, appealed to the Sichuan Provincial Education Department. The Sichuan Provincial Education Department responded to Yang Yimin on June 28, 2005, stating: "Your petition materials have been forwarded to the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau, which has been instructed to respond to you again in accordance with the relevant laws, regulations, policies, and factual basis in force at the time." On August 18, 2005, the office of the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau again made a petition reply to Yang Yimin. The reply stated: "We have again investigated and verified the facts. We have found that the 'Report on the Expulsion of Our Employee Yang Yimin' submitted by the former Chengdu No. 5 Middle School to the former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission in 1992 based on your absenteeism, and the 'Reply to the 'Report on the Expulsion of Our Employee Yang Yimin' from Chengdu No. 5 Middle School' made by the former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission in that year, comply with the provisions of Document Sichuan People's Issue (1984) No. 4 (Chuan Ren Fa (1984) No. 4)." This petition reply was served on Yang Yimin.

On September 9, 2005, the appellant, Yang Yimin, applied for administrative reconsideration with the appellee, the Chengdu Municipal Government, regarding the petition reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau on August 18, 2005, requesting that the reply be annulled or confirmed as illegal, and that the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau be ordered to make a new specific administrative act within a specified time limit. On the same day, the Chengdu Municipal Government, on the grounds that Yang Yimin's application for administrative reconsideration did not meet the acceptance conditions for administrative reconsideration, and pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Administrative Reconsideration Law, made the Decision of Non-Acceptance No. 6 [2005] (Chengfu Fu Bu Zi (2005) No. 6), which was served on Yang Yimin on the 13th of the same month. Yang Yimin, dissatisfied, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court, requesting the annulment of the decision of non-acceptance made by the Chengdu Municipal Government.

The focus of the dispute in the second instance remained: Whether the application for administrative reconsideration filed by the appellant, Yang Yimin, with the appellee, the Chengdu Municipal Government, due to his dissatisfaction with the petition reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau, falls within the scope of acceptance for administrative reconsideration.

The Sichuan High People's Court held in its judgment of second instance:

Article 12 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law provides: "If a party is dissatisfied with a specific administrative act taken by a working department of a local people's government at or above the county level, the party may, at its option, apply for administrative reconsideration either to the people's government at the same level as the department or to the competent department at the next higher level. If a party is dissatisfied with a specific administrative act taken by an administrative organ exercising vertical leadership, such as the customs, financial, state tax, foreign exchange control, or state security organs, the party shall apply for administrative reconsideration to the competent department at the next higher level." Article 17 provides: "Upon receiving an application for administrative reconsideration, the administrative reconsideration organ shall conduct a review within five days. If the application does not comply with the provisions of this Law, it shall decide not to accept the case and shall inform the applicant in writing. If the application complies with the provisions of this Law but is not within the jurisdiction of the organ, it shall inform the applicant to submit the application to the relevant administrative reconsideration organ." According to the above provisions, the Appellee, Chengdu Municipal Government, has the jurisdiction to hear cases where a party, dissatisfied with a specific administrative act taken by its subordinate functional department, applies for administrative reconsideration. After reviewing an application for administrative reconsideration filed by a party, if it finds that the application does not fall within the scope of acceptance under the Administrative Reconsideration Law, it has the authority to make a decision not to accept the case. On September 9, 2005, the Chengdu Municipal Government received the application for administrative reconsideration submitted by the Appellant, Yang Yimin. After review, it found that the application did not meet the conditions for acceptance of administrative reconsideration and issued a decision not to accept the case, which was served on Yang Yimin on September 13 of the same year. The procedure by which the Chengdu Municipal Government made the decision not to accept the case was lawful.

Article 1 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law provides: "This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution for the purpose of preventing and correcting unlawful or inappropriate specific administrative acts, protecting the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations, and ensuring and supervising the lawful exercise of administrative powers by administrative organs." Article 2 provides: "Where a citizen, legal person, or other organization considers that a specific administrative act has infringed upon its lawful rights and interests and submits an application for administrative reconsideration to an administrative organ, and the administrative organ accepts the application for administrative reconsideration and makes a reconsideration decision, this Law shall apply." Article 6 provides: "Under any of the following circumstances, a citizen, legal person, or other organization may apply for administrative reconsideration in accordance with this Law: (1) being dissatisfied with an administrative penalty decision such as a warning, fine, confiscation of illegal gains, confiscation of illegal property, order to suspend production or business, temporary suspension or revocation of a permit, temporary suspension or revocation of a license, or administrative detention; (2) being dissatisfied with a decision on administrative compulsory measures such as restriction of personal freedom, or sealing up, seizing, or freezing property; (3) being dissatisfied with a decision by an administrative organ to alter, suspend, or revoke a certificate such as a permit, license, qualification certificate, or credential; (4) being dissatisfied with a decision by an administrative organ to confirm the ownership or right to use of natural resources such as land, mineral deposits, water flows, forests, mountain ridges, grasslands, wasteland, tidal flats, or sea areas; (5) considering that an administrative organ has infringed upon its lawful right to autonomous operation; (6) considering that an administrative organ has altered or abolished an agricultural contract, thereby infringing upon its lawful rights and interests; (7) considering that an administrative organ has illegally raised funds, collected property, apportioned expenses, or illegally demanded the performance of other obligations; (8) having applied to an administrative organ for the issuance of a certificate such as a permit, license, qualification certificate, or credential, or for the approval or registration of relevant matters, meeting the statutory conditions, but the administrative organ has failed to handle the matter according to law; (9) having applied to an administrative organ for the performance of its statutory duty to protect personal rights, property rights, or the right to education, but the administrative organ has failed to perform such duty according to law; (10) having applied to an administrative organ for the distribution of pension, social insurance funds, or minimum subsistence allowance according to law, but the administrative organ has failed to distribute them according to law; or (11) considering that other specific administrative acts of an administrative organ have infringed upon its lawful rights and interests." According to the above law, a specific administrative act subject to administrative reconsideration refers to an act taken by an administrative subject in the course of exercising its administrative powers, directed at a specific administrative counterpart and concerning a specific matter, which is capable of producing legal effects on the rights and obligations of the administrative counterpart. In this case, the matter on which the Appellant, Yang Yimin, applied for administrative reconsideration was the petition letter reply made by the office of the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau in response to Yang Yimin's complaint. The content of that petition letter reply merely reaffirmed that the "Report on the Removal of Our Employee Yang Yimin" submitted by the former No. 5 Middle School of Chengdu in 1992 and the "Reply to the 'Report on the Removal of Our Employee Yang Yimin' Submitted by No. 5 Middle School of Chengdu" made by the former Chengdu Municipal Education Commission in that same year both complied with the provisions of Document No. 4 [1984] issued by the Sichuan Provincial Personnel Bureau. It did not create any new legal effect on Yang Yimin's rights and obligations. Therefore, it constitutes a repetitive handling act by the administrative organ in response to a complaint filed by a party dissatisfied with a specific administrative act, and consequently is not a specific administrative act subject to administrative reconsideration under the Administrative Reconsideration Law.

The Administrative Reconsideration Law provides a time limit for applying for administrative reconsideration, whereas there is no corresponding statute of limitations for a party to file a complaint with the relevant administrative organ. If the repetitive handling act by which an administrative organ rejects a party's complaint about a specific administrative act were to be regarded as a new specific administrative act, then, regardless of whether the action falls within the statutory time limit, the party could initiate administrative reconsideration proceedings through a complaint, creating a repeating cycle of "complaint—repetitive handling act rejecting the complaint—application for administrative reconsideration against that repetitive handling act—administrative reconsideration or another complaint." This would inevitably render the time limit for applying for administrative reconsideration meaningless, thereby undermining the stability of administrative acts and affecting the lawful administration of administrative organs.

In summary, the petition letter reply made by the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau in response to the complaint of the Appellant, Yang Yimin, is a repetitive handling act by an administrative organ in response to a party's complaint against an administrative act, and does not fall within the scope of acceptance for administrative reconsideration. The decision made by the Appellee, Chengdu Municipal Government, not to accept Yang Yimin's application for administrative reconsideration was correct. The Appellant's ground of appeal that the matter on which he applied for administrative reconsideration meets the conditions for acceptance of administrative reconsideration cannot stand. The judgment of the first instance, which found facts clearly, applied the law correctly, and followed lawful trial procedures, should be affirmed.

Accordingly, in accordance with the provisions of Article 61, Item (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Sichuan High People's Court, on November 21, 2006, hereby adjudicates as follows:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 100 shall be borne by Yang Yimin.

This judgment is final.
